title: NewJeans Returns as Four-Member Group on Fourth Debut Anniversary
excerpt: The K-pop group marked the exact anniversary of their 2022 debut by releasing "2026 Summer of NewJeans" films and photos, confirming Minji's long-awaited return and signaling the start of a new chapter without Danielle.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • NewJeans returns as a quartet with Minji, Hanni, Haerin, and Hyein after their fourth anniversary.
  • Minji's return ends months of speculation regarding her contract negotiations with ADOR.
  • Danielle Marsh is excluded from the new lineup, with an ongoing ₩33 billion lawsuit against her.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=toZQjHykzqA
  • NewJeans released "2026 Summer of NewJeans" films and photos at midnight KST on July 22, confirming the group's return as a quartet of Minji, Hanni, Haerin, and Hyein.
  • Minji's participation confirms her return to ADOR after months of unresolved contract negotiations, ending the biggest question mark over the group's comeback.
  • Danielle Marsh, whose contract was terminated in December 2025, is not part of the new lineup; ADOR's ₩33 billion lawsuit against her remains pending.

NewJeans Breaks Silence With Anniversary Drop

Exactly four years after their surprise debut with "Attention" on July 22, 2022, K-pop group NewJeans announced their return to activity with a coordinated release of films and promotional photos branded "2026 Summer of NewJeans."

> **"But the coordinated nature of the "2026 Summer of NewJeans" rollout, with professional photo shoots and multiple film productions, suggests formal promotions are imminent."** https://x.com/PhilstarNews/status/2079761907393929461

The content dropped at midnight KST on July 22 across the group's official social media channels. Individual photo sets were released for each member — Minji, Hanni, Haerin, and Hyein — alongside five video films and group shots, according to Soompi. The release marks NewJeans' first official group activity since the Seoul Central District Court granted an injunction in March 2025, effectively halting all independent promotions.

The move confirms what had been the subject of intense speculation for months: Minji is back, and NewJeans will proceed as a four-member group.

From Legal Battle to Comeback: The Long Road Back

NewJeans' hiatus stemmed from a bitter management dispute that erupted in 2024. After former ADOR CEO Min Hee-jin — the group's creative architect — was pushed out by parent company HYBE, all five members declared their contracts terminated and briefly rebranded as NJZ.

The rebellion was short-lived. A Seoul court ruled in October 2025 that the contracts with ADOR remained valid through 2029. Haerin and Hyein announced their return to the label in November, followed by Hanni in December. But two members remained in limbo: ADOR terminated Danielle Marsh's contract on December 29, 2025, and filed a ₩43 billion (approximately $29.8 million) damages lawsuit against her, her family, and Min Hee-jin. The claim was later reduced to ₩33 billion ($24.4 million).

Minji's situation was murkier. For months, ADOR would only say negotiations were ongoing. The first public signal came on May 7, 2026 — Minji's birthday — when the group's official accounts posted photos of cookies she had baked for fans, the first time ADOR's channels had acknowledged her since the crisis began.

"Discussions with Minji are generally proceeding in a positive direction."

— ADOR representative, May 2026

The "2026 Summer of NewJeans" release settles the question definitively. With individual content produced for all four members, the return is not a three-member compromise but a full quartet configuration.

Pre-Production Trail: From Copenhagen to Comeback

Signs of a comeback had been building since April, when Hanni, Haerin, and Hyein were spotted in Copenhagen. ADOR confirmed the trio had traveled to the Danish capital with staff for "pre-production to incorporate a new musical narrative." A Copenhagen recording studio was reportedly booked under the ADOR name from April 13 to 17.

Minji was notably absent from the Denmark trip, which fueled fears she might not rejoin the group. Hana Securities analyst Lee Ki-hoon published a report in June projecting that NewJeans would return as a four-member group by October at the latest, calling the group "pivotal" to HYBE's financial outlook. Meritz Securities estimated a four-member comeback could contribute ₩60–70 billion in operating profit in 2026.

"But the coordinated nature of the "2026 Summer of NewJeans" rollout, with professional photo shoots and multiple film productions, suggests formal promotions are imminent."

The Danielle Question

The celebration is bittersweet for many fans. Danielle Marsh — the Korean-Australian member who was part of the original five-member lineup — remains cut off from the group. ADOR alleged that Danielle and her family bore primary responsibility for the members' departure and the delay in their return.

"NewJeans is five or nothing."

— Fan sentiment widely shared on social media

The legal proceedings are still active, with ADOR reducing its damages claim from ₩43 billion to ₩33 billion. Music critic Lim Hee-yun told the BBC during the initial split that with this rupture, "no one wins."

What Comes Next

ADOR has not announced specific comeback plans — no album title, release date, or tour schedule. But the coordinated nature of the "2026 Summer of NewJeans" rollout, with professional photo shoots and multiple film productions, suggests formal promotions are imminent. Industry analysts have pointed to pre-production sessions in Copenhagen as evidence that new music is already in the pipeline.

For the K-pop industry, NewJeans' return is a significant moment. The group topped the Billboard 200, was named IFPI's eighth best-selling artist worldwide in 2023, and became the first girl group in 12 years to win Artist of the Year at the MAMA Awards. Whether the four-member version can recapture that momentum — and what becomes of Danielle's legal battle — will be among the most closely watched storylines in K-pop for the rest of the year.

nri_angle: NewJeans' multicultural lineup — featuring Vietnamese-Australian Hanni and formerly Korean-Australian Danielle — made the group a symbol of diaspora representation in K-pop, and their comeback is being closely watched by South Asian and broader Asian diaspora communities worldwide.
